title: The Field-Line Inspector
summary: Spot impossible magnetic field lines and use zero net flux through closed surfaces.
subject: physics
concepts: Magnetic field lines are closed loops
learningOutcome: The student can tell magnetic field line diagrams from electrostatic ones and from impossible ones, and use zero net magnetic flux through any closed surface.

levels.title: Spot the flaw
levels.adds: Baseline: magnetic lines are closed loops that never cross or end, unlike electric lines (Example 5.3).
hints: Magnetic lines have no beginning or end: look for closed loops.
Lines that start or end on a single point or charge are electrostatic.
Lines that cross, or stop in empty space, are impossible for any field.

levels.title: Closed surface
levels.adds: New idea: the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero (Section 5.3).
hints: Add the fluxes through the known faces, outward positive.
The total through all five faces must be zero.
Keep the sign: the answer can be negative.

levels.title: Through the magnet
levels.adds: More steps: put the surface round one pole, and the lines must carry on inside the magnet (Example 5.4).
hints: The surface is closed, so the total flux is zero.
The lines that leave the outside part must come back in across the cut.
Choose the sign: outward is positive.

misconceptions: Magnetic field lines start on the north pole and end on the south pole
Flux through a closed surface around one pole is not zero
A magnet can be cut to leave a single pole
